title: General composite Buchmann-Lenstra cycle
objective: Implement the real bounded nonidentity-order Buchmann-Lenstra q-radical, multiplier-ring, freeness, and perfect-power cycle with replayable evidence

handoff.summary: Implements a real bounded general-order Buchmann-Lenstra adapter over canonical OrderBasis lattices: tame trace q-radicals, unit-or-split modular kernels, multiplier-ring HNF enlargements, colon and power freeness, Smith-minor obstructions, perfect-power evidence, and deterministic independent replay. A Sage-checked nonidentity quadratic fixture requires two multiplier enlargements before reaching the maximal order.
risks: The trace-radical path deliberately returns resource-error when the unresolved component is not tame at the order degree; small-prime or wild local solvers must handle that branch.
Smith evidence uses an explicit minor-count bound and returns resource-error rather than attempting unbounded high-degree work.

The bootstrapped native addon is absent in this bounded worktree, so native/public-engine tests fail before arithmetic execution with missing sagejs_flint.node; focused dynamic CPython/Sage.js, strict, and architecture checks pass.
next_steps: The integration engine can call buchmann_lenstra_overorder with its current nonidentity OrderBasis; no maximal_order_engine.py change is required for dispatch.
Restart split results on their exact ComponentSplit children and route bounded resource-error results back to certified factor discovery.
Run public engine and native suites in the bootstrapped integration worktree.
